name: TamperEvidentAuditLog
purpose: Append-only record of security-relevant events, hash-chained and signed so any retroactive mutation is detectable by verification.
api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Any

class TamperEvidentAuditLog(Protocol):
    def append(self, actor: str, action: str, resource: str, outcome: str, attributes: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str: ...
    def verify_chain(self, start_seq: int | None = None, end_seq: int | None = None) -> bool: ...
    def get(self, seq: int) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
    def export(self, since_seq: int) -> bytes: ...
invariants: Entries MUST be append-only; the store SHALL reject UPDATE or DELETE on any prior sequence.
Each entry MUST contain the SHA-256 of the prior entry, forming a chain that CANNOT be mutated without detection.
Each entry MUST carry a signature from a key whose private half is NEVER held by the writing service.
Sequence numbers MUST be monotonically increasing with no gaps; verify_chain SHALL fail on gap or regression.
Actor, action, resource, outcome, and timestamp MUST be present on every entry; absence SHALL raise.
Clock source MUST be monotonic server-side; client-supplied timestamps SHALL be rejected.
extension_contract: Downstream targets register a signer adapter (KMS/HSM) and a storage backend (object-lock S3, WORM volume, ledger DB) by implementing the TamperEvidentAuditLog Protocol. Additional attribute fields compose via an attribute-enrichment hook invoked before signing.
consumption_example:
def record_admin_reset(log: TamperEvidentAuditLog, admin_id: str, user_id: str) -> None:
    seq = log.append(
        actor=admin_id,
        action='user.password_reset',
        resource=f'user:{user_id}',
        outcome='success',
        attributes={'via': 'admin_console'},
    )
    assert log.verify_chain(end_seq=None) is True, 'audit chain broke'

sources.source: AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, 2022 revision)
sources.locator: CC7.2 — detection of security events and anomalies
AU-9 Protection of Audit Information; AU-10 Non-repudiation

why_essential: Without a shared chain-verified log, each tool writes its own audit stream and regulators cannot prove evidence integrity; a centralized primitive forces one signed chain per tenant.
alternatives_considered: Per-table shadow columns (updated_by, updated_at) — trivially tamperable by DBA and fails CC7.2 non-repudiation.
Database binlog replay — captures DML but not business actor/outcome and is not signed.
Application log aggregation to SIEM only — breaks on SIEM outage and has no chain verification.
